name: Cookiefy GDPR Compliance
author: cookiefy

sections.description:
Cookiefy provides enterprise-grade GDPR compliance for WordPress websites through an intelligent cookie consent management system. The plugin connects to the Cookiefy service to automatically detect, classify, and manage cookies while providing visitors with proper consent options.

IMPORTANT: This plugin requires connection to external Cookiefy services to function. Please review the “External Services” section below for complete details on data transmission and privacy implications.

Key Features

  • Automatic Cookie Detection – Advanced AI-powered scanning detects all cookies on your website
  • Intelligent Classification – Automatically categorizes cookies (Necessary, Analytics, Marketing, Preferences, Unclassified)
  • Multiple Core Modes – Choose between Standard, Lenient, or Strict blocking based on your needs
  • Premium Banner Themes – Professional designs including Comprehensive and Compact Modern styles
  • Real-time Updates – Cookie settings sync instantly across your website
  • WordPress Integration – Full AJAX support with proper nonce security
  • Custom Configuration – Advanced JSON configuration for power users
  • Performance Optimized – CDN delivery with script preloading for fast load times

Core Modes

Standard Mode (Recommended)
* Balanced GDPR compliance with optimized performance
* Blocks cookies and essential tracking scripts
* Maintains good site compatibility
* Best for most WordPress websites

Lenient Mode (Lightweight)
* Minimal cookie blocking for maximum compatibility
* Only blocks cookie writes – scripts load normally
* Best page performance with reduced privacy protection
* Ideal for complex JavaScript applications or performance-critical sites

Strict Mode (Advanced Users Only)
* Maximum GDPR compliance with comprehensive blocking
* Blocks scripts, DOM modifications, network requests, and localStorage
* May cause website functionality issues
* Only recommended for advanced users who can handle potential breakage

Service Integration

This plugin connects to the Cookiefy external service (https://cookiefy.app) to:
* Retrieve cookie classification data for your domain
* Access banner configuration and translations
* Synchronize consent preferences (optional)
* Provide compliance reporting and analytics

You must create an account at Cookiefy to obtain a Domain ID for the plugin to function. The service processes cookie data according to its privacy policy.

Banner Themes

  • Comprehensive (Recommended) – Feature-rich banner with detailed cookie information and customization options
  • Compact Modern – Clean, minimal design optimized for mobile and desktop

WordPress Features

  • AJAX Integration – Seamless consent handling without page reloads
  • Security First – Proper nonce verification on all AJAX requests
  • Caching Compatible – Works with all major WordPress caching plugins
  • Admin Integration – Full WordPress admin interface with live status updates
  • Consent Logging – Optional compliance logging for audit purposes

External Services

REQUIRED EXTERNAL SERVICE DISCLOSURE

This plugin relies on external services provided by Cookiefy to function. By installing and activating this plugin, you acknowledge that your website will connect to and transmit data to third-party services.

Primary Service: Cookiefy Cookie Management Platform

Service Provider: Cookiefy (cookiefy.app)
Service Purpose: Cookie consent management, cookie classification, and GDPR compliance functionality

What data is sent:
* Your website’s domain name (for service authentication and configuration)
* User consent preferences and timestamps (when users interact with the consent banner)
* Basic website analytics data (page views, consent rates, banner interactions)
* Referrer information and page URLs where consent events occur

When data is sent:
* During plugin initialization (domain verification and configuration retrieval)
* When the consent banner loads on your website
* When users interact with the consent banner (accept, reject, customize)
* When cookies are detected and require classification
* During banner configuration updates in the admin panel

Service endpoints used:
* https://api.cookiefy.app/api/cdn-config/ – Configuration and cookie classification data
* https://api.cookiefy.app/api/cookie-db – Cookie classification database
* https://api.cookiefy.app/api/report-unknown-cookie – Unknown cookie reporting

Legal documentation:
* Terms of Service: https://cookiefy.app/terms-of-service
* Privacy Policy: https://cookiefy.app/privacy-policy

CDN Service: Cookiefy Content Delivery Network

Service Provider: Cookiefy CDN (cdn.cookiefy.app)
Service Purpose: Fast, reliable delivery of consent banner scripts and assets, powered by cloudflare.

What data is sent:
* HTTP requests for JavaScript files and assets
* Standard web server logs (IP address, user agent, referrer)
* Your website’s domain name (in request headers)

When data is sent:
* Every time a visitor loads a page on your website (to fetch banner scripts)
* During initial plugin setup and configuration

CDN endpoints used:
* https://cdn.cookiefy.app/wp-cookiefy-core.min.js – Core cookie blocking, and GDPR compliance functionality
* https://cdn.cookiefy.app/wp-cookiefy-ui.min.js – Standard banner interface
* https://cdn.cookiefy.app/wp-compact-cookiefy-ui-modern.min.js – Compact banner interface

Legal documentation:
* Same as primary service (Cookiefy terms and privacy policy apply)

Data Processing Legal Basis

  • Legitimate Interest: Cookie classification and service delivery
  • Contractual Necessity: Providing the cookie consent management service
  • User Consent: Analytics and reporting features (where applicable)

Data Retention and Geographic Processing

  • Configuration data: Retained for the duration of active service subscription
  • Analytics data: Retained for up to 24 months for reporting purposes
  • User consent records: Retained according to legal requirements (typically 3 years)
  • Processing locations: European Union and United States data centers

Your Control and User Rights

  • Users can request data deletion through the Cookiefy dashboard
  • You can disable analytics collection in the plugin settings
  • The service complies with GDPR, CCPA, and other privacy regulations
  • You can export your consent data through the Cookiefy dashboard

Alternative Solutions

If you prefer not to use external services, consider:
* Self-hosted cookie consent solutions
* WordPress-only cookie plugins (with limited functionality)
* Custom development for your specific requirements

By using this plugin, you acknowledge that:
1. Your website will connect to and transmit data to Cookiefy services
2. You have reviewed and accept Cookiefy’s terms of service and privacy policy
3. You understand the data transmission requirements for the service to function
4. You will inform your website visitors about these external connections as required by law

Support and Documentation

  • Documentation: https://cookiefy.app/en/docs/
  • Support Center: https://cookiefy.app/contact
  • Service Website: https://cookiefy.app

This plugin requires a Domain ID from your Cookiefy account. Sign up for a free trial to get started with enterprise-grade cookie compliance.

Privacy and External Services

This plugin integrates with the Cookiefy service (cookiefy.app) to provide cookie management functionality. When active, the plugin:

  • Connects to Cookiefy CDN servers to load optimized scripts
  • Retrieves cookie classification data and banner configurations
  • May synchronize consent preferences with the service (configurable)
  • Processes Domain ID for service authentication

Data Handling:
* No personal data is transmitted without explicit user consent
* Cookie detection and classification occurs through the external service
* Consent data can be stored locally or optionally synchronized
* All data transmission uses secure HTTPS connections

Required External Connections:
* https://cdn.cookiefy.app/ – For loading optimized banner and core scripts
* https://cookiefy.app/ – For configuration and classification data

The plugin respects user privacy and only processes data necessary for GDPR compliance functionality. Please review Cookiefy’s privacy policy at their website for complete details on data handling practices.

Technical Requirements

  • WordPress 5.0 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • HTTPS recommended for secure cookie handling
  • Domain ID from Cookiefy account
  • JavaScript enabled on visitor browsers

Customisation beyond

It is possible to have a completely custom banner with the blocking script, for more information on how to achieve this, contact support@cookiefy.app
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New in your WordPress admin
  2. Search for “Cookiefy GDPR Compliance”
  3. Click “Install Now” and then “Activate”
  4. Go to Settings > Cookiefy to configure

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin from the WordPress Plugin Directory
  2. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/cookiefy/
  3. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  4. Go to Settings > Cookiefy to configure

Configuration

  1. Sign up at Cookiefy (free trial available)
  2. Add your website domain in the Cookiefy dashboard
  3. Copy your Domain ID from the dashboard (format: domain.com-abc123def456)
  4. Go to Settings > Cookiefy in WordPress
  5. Enable the plugin and paste your Domain ID
  6. Choose your preferred core mode (Standard recommended)
  7. Select your banner theme
  8. Optional: Add custom JSON configuration for advanced features
  9. Save settings and test in a private browser window
sections.faq:
Do I need a Cookiefy account?

Yes, you need an account at cookiefy.app to get your Domain ID and access the cookie management dashboard. A free trial is available.

What data is sent to the Cookiefy service?

The plugin sends your domain name to retrieve cookie classification data and banner configurations. User consent choices can be stored locally or optionally synchronized with the service. No personal data is transmitted without explicit user consent.

What’s the difference between core modes?

Standard Mode: Balanced GDPR compliance with good performance. Blocks cookies and essential tracking scripts while maintaining site compatibility.

Lenient Mode: Lightweight blocking that only prevents cookie writes. Scripts and content load normally for maximum compatibility but with reduced privacy protection.

Strict Mode: Maximum privacy protection with comprehensive blocking of scripts, DOM modifications, network requests, and localStorage. May break website functionality.

Which core mode should I choose?

Choose Standard Mode for most websites – it provides excellent GDPR compliance with good performance. Choose Lenient Mode for sites with complex JavaScript or performance requirements. Only use Strict Mode if you need maximum privacy protection and can handle potential functionality issues.

Will this affect my website performance?

Standard Mode has minimal performance impact. Lenient Mode has virtually no performance impact. Strict Mode may have higher impact due to comprehensive blocking. All modes use CDN delivery with script preloading for optimal performance.

Can I customize the banner appearance?

Yes! Choose from built-in themes in the plugin settings, or use custom JSON configuration and CSS in your Cookiefy dashboard to match your website’s design perfectly.

Is this compatible with caching plugins?

Yes, Cookiefy is fully compatible with all major WordPress caching plugins including WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, and others.

How do I test the installation?

After configuring your settings, visit your website in a private/incognito browser window. The cookie banner should appear automatically. Check the browser console for any error messages during testing.

Can I switch between modes after installation?

Yes, you can change between Standard, Lenient, and Strict modes at any time in the plugin settings. Changes take effect immediately without requiring cache clearing.

Is this fully GDPR compliant?

Standard and Strict modes provide full GDPR compliance. Lenient Mode provides basic cookie consent but may not meet all comprehensive GDPR tracking prevention requirements depending on your specific use case and jurisdiction.
